Mridul came to see me on his own this morning. — Leela

passage: In the school counsellor's room, Tarun's mother sat stiffly with her handbag on her lap. Hafsa Ma'am nodded at Tarun. "Go on. Tell her what you planned." Tarun unfolded a page. "Mummy, I want to go to Aman's house on Saturdays for the science project. Until eight. Here's his address and his mother's number. I'll share my location the whole time. I'll call when I reach, and you or Papa pick me up at eight. Let's try it for one month. If I'm late even once, we stop." His mother read the page twice. "You wrote all this yourself?" "Hafsa Ma'am only helped me put it in order." She looked at the counsellor, then at him. "One month," she said. "And I'm calling Aman's mother tonight." Tarun grinned. "Deal."

qa.q: Until what time did Tarun ask to stay at Aman's?
qa.a: Until eight.

qa.q: What does Tarun's mother sitting stiffly suggest?
qa.a: It suggests she felt tense and wary coming into the meeting, unsure what was being asked.

qa.q: What makes Tarun's proposal a win-win?
qa.a: It gives him Saturdays at Aman's while answering his mother's safety worries with the address, location sharing, a call and pick-up, plus a trial she can end.

qa.q: How does Hafsa Ma'am help without taking over?
qa.a: She encourages Tarun to present it himself and only helped him put it in order, so the plan stays his.

grounding: Shows a teen presenting a conditional one-month trial with address, location sharing, a call on arrival and parent pick-up.
